model_meta.description: Mechanical pressure-relief valve with a spring-loaded ball and pusher; discharge-flow pressure acting across the pusher reduces spring loading as flow increases.

subsystems.description: Outer body with central bore, axially spaced lateral discharge openings and connective opening; rearward end closed by stopper.

ports.name: Connective opening toward sealed control volume

subsystems.description: Forward piece closing the body bore and providing upstream high-pressure chamber, orifice, hemispheric seat/axial well, and downstream chamber.
Ball seated in the hemispheric seat to control fluid passage through the orifice.
Axially sliding pusher without axial fluid through-passage; protrusion contacts the ball, while its face partially throttles discharge openings and separates pressure-exposed volumes.
Spring in the body bore biases the pusher toward contact with the ball and orifice sealing position.
External circuit supplies high-pressure fluid to the upstream chamber; pressure relief is used upon circuit component failure.

item_flows.name: High-pressure fluid into upstream chamber
item_flows.notes: High-pressure circuit supplies valve-piece upstream chamber.

item_flows.name: Discharge pressure communicated to opposite pusher side
item_flows.notes: Connective opening linked with at least one discharge opening exposes the opposite side of the pressure-barrier pusher to discharge pressure.

item_flows.name: Fluid discharged through lateral openings
item_flows.notes: Outlet through lateral discharge openings; destination is unspecified.

steps.description: Below the predetermined upstream pressure threshold, the spring-biased pusher contacts the ball and the ball seals the orifice.
When upstream pressure overcomes the spring loading, the ball moves away from its seat and fluid passes through the orifice into the downstream chamber.
Discharge flow is restricted by the pusher face at lateral openings; pressure in the downstream chamber and the connected opposite-side opening creates a differential across the pusher.
The differential force opposes spring action, reducing spring load on the ball according to discharge flow.
